# Hash Tables in Plain English

## Finding things fast

Searching an unsorted list means checking items one by one, so the work grows with the length of the list. A hash table avoids this by computing where an item belongs. A hash function takes a key, such as a word, and turns it into a number. That number, reduced to fit the table, is the index of a slot in an array.

Looking up a key repeats the same calculation, so the table goes straight to the right slot. On average this takes the same time no matter how many items are stored.

## When keys collide

Two different keys can produce the same slot, which is called a collision. One common fix is chaining, where each slot holds a small list of the entries that landed there. Lookups then scan only that short list instead of the whole table.

As a table fills up, collisions become more frequent and lookups slow down. The share of slots in use is called the load factor. When it passes a set limit, the table allocates a larger array and moves every entry to its new position. This resize is expensive, but it happens rarely enough that the average cost stays low.

cards.title: The problem with lists
cards.body: In an unsorted list you must check items one at a time. The longer the list, the more work each search takes.
cards.quote: Searching an unsorted list means checking items one by one, so the work grows with the length of the list.

cards.title: Keys become positions
cards.body: A hash function turns a key into a number. After being reduced to fit the table, that number points at a slot in an array.
cards.quote: A hash function takes a key, such as a word, and turns it into a number.

cards.title: Why lookups stay quick
cards.body: A lookup runs the same calculation and jumps straight to the slot. The average time does not depend on how many items are stored.
cards.quote: On average this takes the same time no matter how many items are stored.

cards.title: Handling collisions
cards.body: Different keys can map to the same slot. With chaining, each slot keeps a short list, and only that list gets scanned.
cards.quote: One common fix is chaining, where each slot holds a small list of the entries that landed there.

cards.title: Growing the table
cards.body: The load factor measures how full the table is. Past a set limit, the table moves everything into a larger array, which is costly but rare.
cards.quote: When it passes a set limit, the table allocates a larger array and moves every entry to its new position.

quizzes.question: What does a hash function produce from a key?
quizzes.explanation: It turns the key into a number, which is then reduced to a slot index.

quizzes.question: What is a collision?
options: A table running out of memory
Two different keys producing the same slot
A key that is too long
quizzes.explanation: A collision is when two different keys land in the same slot.

quizzes.question: What does the load factor measure?
options: How slow the hash function is
The share of slots in use
quizzes.explanation: The load factor is the share of slots in use.
